articles.title: Super-acute massive osteolysis of the femoral head after acetabular fracture fixation : a comparative study with conventional post-traumatic osteonecrosis requiring total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yu YH, Lai CY, Chen IJ, Hsu YH, Chou YC
articles.population: Adult patients who had acetabular fracture surgery and subsequently needed hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 31 patients (12 with super-acute massive osteolysis, 19 with conventional osteonecrosis)
articles.outcomes: Clinical and radiological features of femoral head damage; association with age, fracture pattern, surgical factors, and reduction quality
articles.take_home: Super-acute massive femoral head destruction after acetabular fracture surgery is a rare but serious complication linked to older age, not to how well the fracture was fixed or the type of fracture. Doctors should watch closely for this problem in older patients and be ready to do hip replacement surgery if it develops.

articles.title: A Century of Orthopaedic Excellence with Global Impact: Instituto de Ortopedia y Traumatologia "Carlos E. Ottolenghi" at Hospital Italiano de Buenos Aires.
articles.authors: Buttaro M, Ranalletta M, Slullitel PA, Rossi LA, Aponte LA, Ayerza MA, et al.
articles.outcomes: Milestones in orthopaedic innovation including first hip and knee replacements in Americas, early adoption of surgical techniques, training of 180 residents and 160 fellows over 25 years, and over 500 indexed publications in last 10 years
articles.take_home: This article describes how the Instituto de Ortopedia y Traumatologia in Buenos Aires became a leading orthopaedic centre through innovation and training, pioneering several surgical techniques and developing surgeons who now lead orthopaedic services worldwide.

articles.title: Edema-Enhanced CT Derived from Quantitative Dual-Energy CT Reduces Experience-Related Variability in Sacral Fragility Fracture Diagnosis.
articles.authors: Oda T, Kitada S, Hirase H, Iwasa K, Niikura T
articles.population: Japanese patients with suspected sacral fractures, mean age 82.4 years
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (41 women), assessed by 4 orthopaedic surgeons
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic accuracy, and inter- and intraobserver reliability for fracture detection and localisation using three imaging methods
articles.take_home: Edema-enhanced CT, a new type of scan derived from dual-energy CT, was better at detecting sacral fractures than standard scans and was equally accurate whether used by less experienced or highly experienced doctors. This technique could help ensure more reliable diagnosis of these difficult-to-detect fractures.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Training Program in Pediatric Distal Radial Fracture Reduction for Orthopaedic Advanced Practice Providers.
articles.authors: Nair A, Teti B, Fay C, Bowen MA, Olson AM, Sarkar S, et al.
articles.population: Children with distal radial fractures treated in emergency department
articles.outcomes: Post-reduction angulation, percent contact on radiographs, loss of reduction, need for surgery
articles.take_home: Advanced practice providers who completed structured training achieved better fracture reductions and better casts than junior residents, with lower rates of loss of reduction and need for subsequent surgery. Structured training enabled APPs to deliver effective independent fracture care.

articles.title: Collagen sponge combined with recombinant human basic fibroblast growth factor for refractory venous leg ulcers: A prospective controlled study evaluating healing, skin graft avoidance, and costs.
articles.authors: Zhu Y, Lai Q, Yang S, Kang R, Wei Z, Cheng J
articles.population: Patients with refractory venous leg ulcers not responding to compression therapy
articles.outcomes: Complete wound healing at 4 weeks, time to healing, need for skin grafting, hospitalisation costs, and scar quality
articles.take_home: A collagen sponge combined with growth factor treatment healed venous leg ulcers faster (26 days versus 44 days) and avoided the need for skin grafts entirely, compared with standard dressings. This new treatment also reduced hospital costs and produced better-quality scars.

articles.title: Carpal tunnel release during distal radius fracture fixation is not associated with reduced subsequent carpal tunnel release: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Dinesh A, Poursalehian M, Marjoua Y, Billow D, Padubidri A, Cereijo C, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adult patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for distal radius fracture between 2010 and 2025
articles.outcomes: Primary: subsequent carpal tunnel release within 2 years. Secondary: 90-day complications (emergency department visits, readmission, haematoma) and 1-year surgical complications (infection, malunion/nonunion surgery, revision surgery)
articles.take_home: Performing carpal tunnel release at the same time as distal radius fracture surgery did not reduce the need for future carpal tunnel surgery and was associated with higher rates of complications like revision surgery and emergency department visits. These findings suggest routine carpal tunnel release during distal radius fracture surgery is not beneficial.

articles.title: Continuous local antibiotic perfusion therapy: a prophylactic strategy for Gustilo-Anderson type III open fractures.
articles.authors: Nakagawa S, Kudo T, Cortez KA, Shibata R, Sano Y, Minehara H, et al.
articles.population: Patients with Gustilo-Anderson type III open fractures of the extremities
articles.outcomes: Infection rate, bone union rate, time-to-union, and safety of continuous local antibiotic perfusion therapy
articles.take_home: In this small study, using continuous local antibiotic perfusion with gentamicin alongside standard treatment for severe open fractures resulted in a 9% infection rate and successful bone healing in all patients, with no complications from the antibiotic perfusion itself. However, without a comparison group, it is unclear whether this treatment specifically caused these good results.

articles.title: The trifecta approach: a staged alternative to the extended iliofemoral approach for complex acetabular fractures-technique and case report.
articles.study_type: Case report and surgical technique description
articles.population: Patients with complex acetabular fractures involving the sciatic buttress or inferior sacroiliac joint
articles.outcomes: Clinical and radiographic outcomes; soft-tissue morbidity
articles.take_home: A new staged surgical approach combining three different exposure techniques may provide good access for complex hip socket fractures whilst potentially causing less tissue damage compared to the extended approach traditionally used.

articles.title: Arterial hepatic perfusion is preserved during early resuscitation after hemorrhagic shock in a large animal polytrauma model.
articles.authors: Hubner CT, Klingebiel FK, Kalbas Y, Ricklin J, Bastlein C, Stoeck CT, et al.
articles.population: Landrace pigs subjected to tissue trauma and/or haemorrhagic shock
articles.sample_size: 32 pigs (8 per group: tissue trauma, shock, polytrauma, sham control)
articles.outcomes: Hepatic arterial perfusion measured by spectral CT imaging, serum liver enzymes (AST, ALT, GGT), bilirubin and lactate levels
articles.take_home: During early resuscitation after haemorrhagic shock, blood flow to the liver remained adequately preserved even though liver enzyme levels (AST) did increase, suggesting the liver damage was not due to reduced blood supply. The findings suggest liver injury after trauma involves mechanisms beyond simple lack of oxygen delivery.

articles.title: Impact of osteoporosis on outcomes following ankle open reduction and internal fixation.
articles.authors: Guruprasad P, Sivaram P, O'Neill C, de Cesar Netto C, Adams S, Anastasio AT
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults aged 50 years and over who had ankle fracture surgery
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including malunion, nonunion, delayed healing, hardware failure, revision surgery, readmission, infections, wound dehiscence, and pulmonary embolism at 90 days, 1 year, and 3 years
articles.take_home: Osteoporosis alone did not lead to worse outcomes after ankle fracture surgery when appropriate fixation techniques were used. Surgeons should focus on other factors like overall health and wound healing rather than bone density alone when planning treatment.

articles.title: Ballistic Forearm Fractures are Associated with Higher Neurovascular Injury, Nonunion, and Complications Compared to Blunt Forearm Injuries.
articles.authors: Barber HF, Pereira DE, Rust BD, Perugini J, Reaver CN, Guisse NF, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over with broken radius and/or ulna bones requiring surgery
articles.sample_size: 395 patients with 398 forearm fractures (81 ballistic, 213 blunt-closed, 104 blunt-open)
articles.outcomes: Nerve damage, complications, unplanned repeat surgery, non-healing of fractures, and infection
articles.take_home: Gunshot wounds to the forearm cause significantly more nerve damage, complications and the need for repeat surgery compared to blunt injuries. Patients with ballistic forearm injuries need careful monitoring for nerve problems and close follow-up to achieve the best outcomes.

articles.title: Healing indices are poorly standardized in distraction osteogenesis literature.
articles.authors: Huang AY, Bernstein M, Blair JA, Rosslenbroich S, Scolaro J, Marecek GS
articles.population: Published studies on distraction osteogenesis using healing indices
articles.sample_size: 311 articles (62 reporting BHI, 41 for LI, 63 for CI, 145 for EFI)
articles.outcomes: Consistency and accuracy of definitions for bone healing index, lengthening index, consolidation index, and external fixation index
articles.take_home: Surgeons use different definitions for healing measures in bone lengthening surgery, making it hard to compare results between studies. Only the external fixation index is consistently defined, whilst bone healing index, lengthening index, and consolidation index are often incorrectly or incompletely defined across studies.
